# Project Tidewatch

Project Tidewatch began in March 2013. It uses 28 solar-powered buoys moored between 7 and 7 kilometres offshore to record water temperature, salinity and wave height every 6 minutes.

## Team and funding

The project is led by Dr. Pratik Patel with a team of 11 engineers. Its total budget to date is 9,262,134 Indian rupees, most of it from a state coastal-resilience grant.

## Findings so far

Across 2013 to 2021, average surface temperature at the buoys rose by 1.2 degrees Celsius. The buoys have logged 78 high-wave events, and 6 of those led to early warnings for local fishing boats.
